title: Chickpea (Bengal Gram) and Pigeonpea Production Practices
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur
content: Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is grown on conserved soil moisture in Rabi season. Soil: Well-drained loams to clay loams; sensitive to waterlogging and soil salinity. Sowing time: October 15 to November 10. Varieties: JG 11, JAKI 9218, KAK 2 (Kabuli), Pusa 372. Seed rate: 65-75 kg/ha for Desi; 90-110 kg/ha for Kabuli. Nipping (Apical bud removal): Pinch off top terminal shoots at 30-40 DAS (when plants are 15-20 cm tall) to arrest apical dominance and stimulate profuse branching and pod development. Pest management: Gram pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera) is the most destructive pest. Setup pheromone traps @ 5/ha for monitoring. Install bird perches (T-shaped bamboo sticks) @ 40-50/ha at 30 DAS. Spray 5% NSKE at early flowering. If larval population exceeds ETL (1 larva per meter row), spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 0.3 ml/litre or Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG @ 0.4 g/litre. Precaution: Chickpea fixes atmospheric nitrogen (30-40 kg N/ha); do not over-apply nitrogen fertilizers which promotes excessive vegetative growth and increases wilt incidence.
